# bible-mode-b test: system reference

Status: UPDATED FOR CODE CHANGES (claude/update-125-126, 2026-11-24; 11 cards written or rewritten in the catalog and queue modules and the pages that cite them changed, not re-verified; `ledger/delta.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` name every file and function). Before this update the status was: CORRECTED AFTER VERIFICATION (report of 2026-11-24, round 6; about 250 statements, rows, citations and diagram elements added or changed since (an estimate from the edits listed in `revision-log.md`), not re-verified, each accounted for in `revision-log.md`).

| Coverage | `coverage.py` of 2026-11-24, after the update for the code changes: result PASS at deep, 124/124 symbols, 103/103 functions with a full card, 344/344 branch lines, 247/247 call-graph edges, 3,583/3,583 citations (one per range), 17/17 front-matter pages, 2/2 calls into other components |

## In two minutes

The repository combines a sample catalog/orders application with a separate GitHub Actions workflow system for producing and maintaining codebase analyses; the modules share a repository but are not one deployed service (`README.md:1-7`; [`system context`](hld/01-system-context.md)). The catalog keeps product records in process memory, provides price and stock lookups, and includes an optional HTTP server (`components/catalog/catalog.py:11-41`; `components/catalog/service.py:15-49`). The current order helpers import the catalog directly, while the HTTP price client is intended for a separately deployed orders service (its docstring says so) and is called only by tests in this repository (inferred: its docstring, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4`, names the separate-service use, and a search of the repository finds `catalog_client` imported only by `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py`) (`components/orders/orders.py:5`, `components/orders/orders.py:19-20`, `components/orders/orders.py:35-42`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-4`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`). Orders computes totals, validates stock, and sends settlement requests to a partner or local development endpoint (`components/orders/orders.py:19-51`). The `bible-mode-b` queue uses GitHub issues, branches, and pull requests to assign Copilot work, inspect artifacts, and coordinate human review (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:128-154`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:167-174`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:970-995`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:867-871`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:705-756`). The `tools` commands generate a component plan, validate component artifacts, and create component issues (`tools/plan.py:21-58`; `tools/gate.py:42-78`; `tools/fanout.sh:7-30`). GitHub Actions runs the queue and related automation on `ubuntu-latest` runners (assumed: GitHub-hosted runners) (`.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:19-37`); no production deployment topology for catalog or orders is declared (inferred: a listing of the 30 files outside the analysis folder and the skills shows no Dockerfile, compose file, Procfile, deployment manifest, service unit or build file, and a search of them for `dockerfile`, `docker-compose`, `procfile`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `terraform` and `systemd` finds 0 hits; [`architecture`](hld/02-architecture.md)). The main operational cautions are the plain-HTTP payment call (the supplier feed now uses HTTPS with a verifying context, but the live supplier certificate was not checked (inferred: per `https-migration/https-migration-summary.md:29`)), unauthenticated catalog routes (inferred: a search of `components` for `auth`, `authorization`, `login`, `password`, `token` and `jwt` finds 0 hits), process-local product data, and no source evidence for the supplier feed's claimed nightly schedule (inferred: a search of the repository outside the analysis folder and the skills for `cron` and `schedul` finds 3 hits, the docstring at `components/catalog/catalog.py:49` and the queue's own schedule at `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:8-9`, and a search for `fetch_supplier_feed` finds its definition and one test call) (`components/catalog/catalog.py:8`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:48-63`; `components/catalog/service.py:24-43`; `components/orders/orders.py:7-12`, `components/orders/orders.py:45-50`).

## How to run

- One component: `python3 -I .github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/scripts/next.py --repo . --analysis codebase-analysis --component NAME --new-session`, then follow what it prints until `COMPONENT DONE NAME`.
- Where every component stands: `python3 -I .github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/scripts/next.py --repo . --analysis codebase-analysis --board`.
- On GitHub without workflows: one issue per component from `ledger/issues/` (docs/github-guide.md, Part 4).
- When every component is done: the assemble step (`ledger/issues/assemble.md`).

# Architecture

The application is a small Python library with a standard-library HTTP server; the repository also contains command-line analysis tools and GitHub Actions adapters. No application image, package build, deployment manifest, service manager, or production topology is declared (inferred: a listing of the 30 files outside the analysis folder and the skills shows no Dockerfile, compose file, Procfile, manifest, service unit or build file, and a search of them for `dockerfile`, `docker-compose`, `procfile`, `kubernetes`, `helm`, `terraform` and `systemd` finds 0 hits). GitHub Actions runs the Mode B scripts on `ubuntu-latest` runners (assumed: GitHub-hosted runners). The TLS migration inventory and service configuration are repository configuration artifacts, not deployed services (`tls-migration/evidence/inventory.json:1-14`; `tls-migration/tls-services.yaml:1-20`). The records of the supplier-feed HTTPS migration under `https-migration/` (`changed-files.txt`, `https-allowlist.txt`, `https-inventory.md`, `https-migration-summary.md`, `tests-before.txt`, `tests-after.txt`) are documents and test output, not code that runs; they list the files the change touched, the 11 tests that passed afterwards (9 before), and the one endpoint still on HTTP, the payment partner (`https-migration/changed-files.txt:1-8`, `https-migration/tests-before.txt:3`, `https-migration/tests-after.txt:3`, `https-migration/https-migration-summary.md:11-17`).

## Record lifecycles

### GitHub issue

The queue creates an open issue, updates its body/labels/assignment while it is active, and closes it either as completed or not planned. A retry is a new issue with an incremented attempt, not a reopening of the failed issue. A pull request that says "Fixes #N" closes the issue when GitHub merges it (assumed: GitHub behaviour, stated in the comment at `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1038-1039`).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Open : create_issue
  Open --> Open : assign, comment, label, update body
  Open --> ClosedCompleted : close(reason=completed)
  Open --> ClosedNotPlanned : first failure, release, or a whole verification that asked for corrections
  ClosedCompleted --> [*]
  ClosedNotPlanned --> [*] : retry creates a new issue
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `create_issue` starts tracker and session records | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:167-174`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:767-768`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:793-794`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:900-908`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1420` |
| Issue body, assignment and label updates | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:333-353`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:623-628` |
| Normal close reason defaults to `completed` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:343-344` |
| A first failed attempt closes as `not_planned` and an attempt-2 issue is created; a second failure stays open, labelled `bible-needs-human` and unassigned, with a comment | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:642-661` |
| A component session a person released is closed as `not_planned`; a verify-all issue that the queue still sees open, when its merged pull request holds a report that asks for corrections, is also closed as `not_planned` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:618-622`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1095-1099` |

### Agent session pull request

Chunk and verify session PRs are merged into a component branch after path and status checks; failed PRs are closed. The PRs of the plan, assembly, whole-verification, whole-revision and update sessions target the default branch and a person merges them, since the queue never merges into the default branch (inferred: the module docstring, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, says so, and a search of the queue for `.merge(` finds 1 call, at `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965`, for session pull requests into the component branch). The separate component review PR also targets the default branch and is merged by a person, not by this queue (inferred: the same two sources).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> Draft : Copilot opens session PR
  [*] --> Ready : Copilot opens it as non-draft
  Draft --> Ready : ready(pr)
  Ready --> MergedToComponentBranch : merge(pr)
  Ready --> MergedByPerson : a person merges a session PR into the default branch
  Draft --> Closed : failure closes PR
  Ready --> Closed : failure closes PR
  MergedToComponentBranch --> [*]
  MergedByPerson --> [*]
  Closed --> [*]
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Agent may open draft; `merge` marks it ready (through `ready`, a GraphQL mutation) before it merges; a PR that is not a draft needs no such step and counts as asked for review | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:355-363`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:365-369`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:588` |
| Queue validates changed files and status before merging a chunk or verify session PR into the component branch | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:931-965` |
| Plan, assemble, verify-all, revise-all and update sessions are assigned with the default branch as base, and the queue never merges into it (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:768`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1129`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1249`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1380` |
| A person merges those session pull requests into the default branch (`Ready --> MergedByPerson`) (inferred: the module docstring says "a person merges those pull requests", and the queue only reads `merged_at` for them) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1086-1087`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1199-1200` |
| Failed session closes its PR | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:645-647` |

### Component review pull request

The separate component review PR targets the default branch and is merged by a person, not by this queue (inferred: the module docstring, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, and `merge` is called only at `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965`, for session pull requests into the component branch).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> ReviewOpen : create component PR
  ReviewOpen --> MergedByPerson : human merges to default branch
  ReviewOpen --> ClosedUnmerged : closed without merging
  MergedByPerson --> [*]
  ClosedUnmerged --> [*]
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Component review PR is opened for a person to review (its description says "Review the pages under ... then merge") | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:867-871`; module docstring `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28` |
| A matching PR closed without merging stops the component with "needs a person" until it is reopened or a new run starts | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:805-807` |

### Component row on the tracker

The tracker issue shows one row per component, recomputed from GitHub at every check, so the arrows below are the usual order of rows across checks (inferred: no row is stored, `Queue.run` builds each one again from the issues and pull requests it finds).

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> NOT_STARTED : no issue of this run carries the component label
  NOT_STARTED --> SESSION_STARTING : a chunk is assigned within the concurrency cap
  SESSION_STARTING --> RUNNING : the session's pull request shows Copilot working
  RUNNING --> SESSION_MERGED : a finished session is merged
  RUNNING --> WAITING_ANSWERS : a finished chunk session reports WAITING_ANSWER
  WAITING_ANSWERS --> RUNNING : the answer is given and Copilot works again
  SESSION_MERGED --> SESSION_STARTING : the next check assigns a chunk
  SESSION_MERGED --> RUNNING : the next check assigns a verification, shown at once as verify running
  SESSION_STARTING --> NEEDS_PERSON : a hold such as a refused start or a second failure
  RUNNING --> NEEDS_PERSON : a hold such as a second failure
  NEEDS_PERSON --> RELEASED : a person removes the label bible-needs-human
  RELEASED --> SESSION_STARTING : the next check decides from the current state
  SESSION_MERGED --> REVIEW : an accepted report with a matching fingerprint opens the review pull request
  REVIEW --> NEEDS_PERSON : the pull request is closed without merging
  REVIEW --> MERGED : a person merges it
  MERGED --> [*]
```

| Element | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| `not started` when no issue of this run carries the component label; a chunk is then assigned while the `concurrency` cap allows | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:820-821`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:747-751` |
| `<kind> running`, and `waiting for answers on #<PR>` for a finished chunk session whose status is `WAITING_ANSWER` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:584-586`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:923-924`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:943-947` |
| `waiting for answers` returns to `<kind> running` when the session's pull request shows Copilot working again; the answer is given on the pull request with `@copilot` (the label text) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:104`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:584-586`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:923-924` |
| A finished session that passes the checks is merged and shown as `<kind> merged`; the next check assigns the next chunk (shown as `session starting`) or the verification (shown at once as `verify running`) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965-968`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:860-861`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:899-909` |
| `needs a person` after a hold (a second failure, a refused start, the session cap or the verification rounds used up) | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:648-653`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:917-919`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:849-858`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:886-894` |
| `released: next step at the next check` after a person removes `bible-needs-human` | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:618-622`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:812-813` |
| A report that `accepted` counts as verified (a `PASS`, or a `PASS AFTER CORRECTIONS` with a confirmed re-check), with a matching fingerprint, opens the review pull request; a person merges it (inferred: the module docstring, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, and `merge` is called only at `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965`), or it is closed without merging | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:867-871`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:803-807` |

The component status artifact also carries `NEW_CHAT`, `COMPONENT_DONE`, `WAITING_ANSWER`, and `STOP`; this repository code reads these values to decide queue behavior but does not write their transitions (inferred: a search of the queue for `/contents` finds 1 hit, the read in `file`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:195-199`) (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:73`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:552-555`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:830-832`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:941-951`). The transitions belong to the analysis toolkit and are not inferred here.

| Tracker `bible-settings` block | `Queue.reconcile` reads it through `settings_of`, and `Queue.run` passes it on | `start` writes it when it creates the tracker, and `Queue.render` writes it back with each table rewrite | A hidden JSON comment in the tracker body; a tracker with no readable or unsafe block is skipped with a log line | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:86`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:407-427`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:668-671`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1313`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1420` |

When a person closes the tracker, or the run does not finish, `Queue.replay_closed_runs` replays them at a later check: it reads the paths of every closed tracker that has no `bible-replayed` label and no mark comment, passes them to `Queue.delta` (which records them on a run open at that time, or creates the update issues), comments with `REPLAYED_MARK` and labels the tracker `bible-replayed` (inferred: a search of the file for `deferred_updates(` finds 4 hits, the definition and three calls, two at the Done step and one in `replay_closed_runs`). # Key flows

| # | Flow | Trigger | Components | Endpoint cards |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Start an analysis run | Operator dispatches `bible-plan` | GitHub Actions, `bible_queue.py`, GitHub | None |
| 2 | Queue creates and assigns the planning session | Queue schedule or manual dispatch | `bible_queue.py`, GitHub, Copilot | None |
| 3 | Component session passes the gate and reaches human review | Agent session PR and `COMPONENT_DONE` status | Queue, toolkit gate, Copilot, reviewer | None |
| 4 | Whole-analysis assembly and verification | All component review PRs are merged | Queue, assembly agent, verification agent, reviewer | None |
| 5 | Changed code produces component delta issues | Default-branch push | Delta workflow, queue, GitHub, Copilot | None |
| 6 | Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog | Python caller invokes order functions | `orders`, `catalog` | None |
| 7 | Remote catalog client reads a price | Python caller or HTTP client test | `catalog_client`, catalog HTTP service | [Catalog API](../lld/api/catalog/catalog.md) |
| 8 | Settlement sends an order amount | Python caller invokes `settle` | `orders`, payment partner or local fake | None |
| 9 | Component plan, fanout and gate | Local operator runs the tools | `plan.py`, `fanout.sh`, `gate.py`, GitHub CLI | None |
| 10 | POC workflow creates and assigns a task issue | Operator dispatches the POC workflow | GitHub Actions, `gh`, GitHub, Copilot | None |

## 1. Start an analysis run

**Trigger:** An operator dispatches `bible-plan` from the default branch. **Outcome:** The workflow creates one tracker issue with the run settings; the queue starts the planning session on its next run.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Repository operator
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible-queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  Operator->>Actions: Dispatch bible-plan with model and component inputs
  Actions->>Queue: Run start with GH_TOKEN and workflow inputs
  Queue->>Queue: Check GITHUB_REPOSITORY and GH_TOKEN, then validate model and component arguments
  alt a variable is missing or an argument is refused
    Note over Queue,Actions: Exit with the refusal message, no label or tracker is created
  else accepted
    Queue->>API: Ensure labels
    alt a run is already open, or the settings are refused
      Note over Queue,Actions: Exit with the refusal message, no tracker is created
    else accepted
      Queue->>API: Create tracker issue with settings JSON
      API-->>Queue: Tracker issue number
      Queue-->>Actions: Print tracker number and queue-start guidance
    end
  end
  Actions-->>Operator: Report workflow result
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator dispatches the workflow and supplies the inputs. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-23` |
| 2 | Workflow checks the default branch (the job's `if:` condition), verifies `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN`, and invokes `start`. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:36`, `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:40-54` |
| 3 | `main` exits unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` and `GH_TOKEN` are set, then validates the model and component arguments. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1400-1402`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1407-1411` |
| 4 | Queue ensures labels (before either refusal), refuses an open tracker and refused settings, and then creates a tracker issue with settings in a hidden JSON comment. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1412-1420` |
| 5 | GitHub returns the tracker issue number. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1420-1421` |
| 6 | CLI prints the issue number and queue-start guidance. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1421-1422` |
| 7 | Workflow reports its result to the operator. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:50-54` |

**Failure paths:** A non-default branch skips the job (`if:` at line 36); missing secret exits with an error; invalid models, components, missing repository/token settings, or an already-open tracker terminate `start` rather than creating a second run (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:36`, `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:52-54`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1400-1419`).

heading_path: 2. Queue creates and assigns the planning session
text:
## 2. Queue creates and assigns the planning session

**Trigger:** The 15-minute schedule or a manual queue dispatch. **Outcome:** Reconciliation reads GitHub state and opens/assigns the next planning issue.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible-queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Actions->>Queue: Run reconcile from default-branch checkout
  Queue->>API: List open tracker issues
  API-->>Queue: Tracker and hidden settings
  Queue->>Queue: Read components.json and select planning phase
  Queue->>API: Read planning issue text
  API-->>Queue: Issue template
  Queue->>Queue: Build the assignment with the configured model
  Queue->>API: Create planning issue, assigning Copilot in the same request
  API-->>Agent: Deliver issue assignment
  Agent-->>API: Open planning PR
  alt Copilot refuses to start
    Queue->>API: Label needs-human, unassign and comment the reason
  else no PR 30 minutes after assignment
    Queue->>API: Close the issue and open attempt 2, or hold after the second failure
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | The queue workflow starts on schedule or manual dispatch and checks out the default branch. | `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:7-10`, `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:23-37` |
| 2 | `reconcile` lists open tracker issues. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:152-154`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:667` |
| 3 | GitHub returns the tracker and its hidden settings. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:142-154`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:407-427` |
| 4 | Queue loads `components.json` and selects planning when the catalog is missing, proposed, or invalid. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:716-718` |
| 5 | Queue reads the planning issue text from `ledger/issues/plan.md`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:762-766` |
| 6 | GitHub returns the issue template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:195-199`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:438-444` |
| 7 | Queue builds the assignment: the target repository, the base branch and, when one is set, the configured analysis model. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:447-451`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:768` |
| 8 | Queue creates the planning issue; the same create request assigns Copilot (its payload carries `assignees` and `agent_assignment`), so there is no separate assign call. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:170-174`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:767-768` |
| 9 | GitHub delivers the issue assignment to Copilot (assumed: GitHub performs the assignment named in the request). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:171-174` |
| 10 | Agent work and PR status return through GitHub issue timelines and pull requests. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:205-235`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:577-593` |

**Failure paths:** An unreadable tracker settings block is logged and skipped; a per-tracker exception does not stop reconciliation of other trackers. A detected start error creates a human hold; a no-PR timeout retries once, then requires a person (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:669-675`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:774-778`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:634-661`).

heading_path: 3. Component session passes the gate and reaches human review
text:
## 3. Component session passes the gate and reaches human review

**Trigger:** Component work produces a session PR and a `COMPONENT_DONE` status. **Outcome:** A matching accepted verification opens a component review PR to the default branch.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  participant API as GitHub
  participant Queue as bible-queue.py
  participant Gate as coverage.py and status.py
  actor Reviewer as Repository reviewer
  Agent->>API: Open chunk PR with component pages and status
  Queue->>API: Read PR files and status at PR head
  alt disallowed files, no progress or STOP
    Queue->>API: Close the PR and open attempt 2, or hold for a person
  end
  Queue->>API: Merge accepted session PR into component branch
  Queue->>API: Read component status from branch
  Queue->>API: Download component branch tarball
  Queue->>Gate: Check coverage and calculate page fingerprint
  Gate-->>Queue: Gate result and fingerprint
  alt gate fails
    Queue->>API: Create the next chunk issue, or hold at the session cap
  end
  Queue->>API: Create verification issue assigned on the verification model
  Agent->>API: Open verification PR with report
  Queue->>API: Read report and merge accepted verification PR
  alt accepted report (PASS, or PASS AFTER CORRECTIONS with a confirmed re-check) and the fingerprint matches the checked pages
    Queue->>API: Create component review PR against default branch
  else a report was read, no chunk since it, and two verifications without an accepted report
    Queue->>API: Create a hold issue for a person
  else corrections asked about these pages, and no chunk since the verification
    Queue->>API: Create a revision chunk issue
  else no report, or the fingerprint does not match the pages
    Queue->>API: Create a new verification issue
  end
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge component PR
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Queue finds the agent's open chunk PR and checks the PR's changed files. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:568-574`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:914`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:925-940` |
| 2 | Queue validates changed paths and reads status JSON at the PR head. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:931-941` |
| 3 | A valid session PR is marked ready if draft, merged into the component branch, and its issue is closed. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:355-369`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965-968` |
| 4 | Queue reads the merged component status; on `COMPONENT_DONE`, it starts the gate. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:830-835` |
| 5 | Queue unpacks the branch tarball in a temporary directory. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:292-331`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:976-979` |
| 6 | Queue runs coverage and fingerprint checks using scripts from the configured toolkit path. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:972-990` |
| 7 | Gate returns its pass/fail result and page fingerprint. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:987-990` |
| 8 | Queue creates a verification issue assigned on `verify_model`; `start` refuses a `--verify-model` that equals `--model` (inferred: a search of `bible_queue.py` for `verify_model` finds 6 hits, and only line 1407 compares it with `model`). When the last report's verdict is `PASS AFTER CORRECTIONS` with an accuracy of at least 95, the verification issue ends with `RECHECK_ASK`, the request to re-check what that report flagged instead of drawing a new sample. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:899-909`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:510-520`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1407-1408` |
| 9 | Verification agent opens a PR containing the verification report. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:911-914`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:962-964` |
| 10 | Queue merges the eligible verification PR and reads its verdict, major corrections, re-check count, accuracy and fingerprint. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:965-968`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:478-507`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:865-866` |
| 11 | A report that `accepted` counts as verified (a `PASS`, or a `PASS AFTER CORRECTIONS` with a confirmed re-check) whose fingerprint matches the checked pages creates a PR for a person to review. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:523-542`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:867-871` |
| 12 | Human reviewer merges the component PR to the default branch (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:803-804` |

**Failure paths:** Disallowed PR files, `STOP`, no progress, missing verification report, or a revision that does not reach `COMPONENT_DONE` triggers the one-retry/hold logic. `WAITING_ANSWER` labels the issue and PR. A failed gate starts more component work; a report with corrections that is not accepted, an unreadable or stale fingerprint, or repeated unaccepted verification leads to revision, re-verification, or a human hold (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:642-661`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:931-964`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:841-898`).

## 4. Whole-analysis assembly and verification

**Trigger:** Component review PRs have been merged. **Outcome:** Assembly and a second-model verification are merged; an accepted whole-analysis report that is about the pages now, and was written by this run's own pull request, closes the tracker. A report that is not accepted starts one revision of the whole analysis and then a second verification; after two whole verifications without an accepted, current report a person decides.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Reviewer as Repository reviewer
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible-queue.py
  participant API as GitHub
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Reviewer->>API: Merge all component review PRs
  Actions->>Queue: Run scheduled reconcile
  Queue->>Queue: Select whole-system assembly phase
  Queue->>API: Read assembly issue template
  API-->>Queue: Assembly template
  Queue->>API: Create and assign assembly issue
  Agent->>API: Open assembly PR with whole-system pages
  alt session ended before status.json was written
    Queue->>API: Comment @copilot continue on the PR (at most 3 times)
  end
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge assembly PR
  Queue->>API: Close assembly issue and create verify-all issue
  Agent->>API: Open verification PR with whole-analysis report
  alt session ended before verification-report.md was written
    Queue->>API: Comment @copilot continue on the PR (at most 3 times)
  end
  Reviewer->>API: Review and merge verification PR
  Queue->>API: Read verdict and validate report
  alt accepted report, this run's PR, fingerprint equals the pages now
    Queue->>API: Create update issues for the paths recorded while the run was open
    Queue->>API: Post Done and close the tracker
    Queue->>API: Create update issues for paths recorded after the first read
    Queue->>API: Post the replayed mark and label the tracker bible-replayed
  else corrections asked
    Queue->>API: Label the verification issue bible-needs-revision
    Queue->>API: Create a revise-all issue at the next check
    Agent->>API: Open revision PR for the whole analysis
    alt session ended before status.json was written
      Queue->>API: Comment @copilot continue on the PR (at most 3 times)
    end
    Reviewer->>API: Review and merge revision PR
    Queue->>API: Create the next verify-all issue
  else accepted report about other pages, or not by this run
    Queue->>API: Label the verification issue bible-stale-verdict
    Queue->>API: Create the next verify-all issue, no revision
  else two whole verifications without an accepted current report
    Queue->>API: Create a hold issue for a person
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Component PRs are merged by a person; scripts do not merge work to the default branch (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:28`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:803-804` |
| 2 | Queue workflow invokes reconciliation. | `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:7-10`, `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:23-37` |
| 3 | Queue selects the whole-system assembly phase when every wanted component's row is `merged`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:754-755` |
| 4 | Queue reads the assembly issue template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1119-1120` |
| 5 | GitHub returns the assembly template. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:438-444` |
| 6 | Queue creates and assigns the assembly issue. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1128-1130` |
| 7 | Assembly agent opens a PR with whole-system pages. When its session has ended but the PR does not yet contain the assembly's `status.json`, the queue comments `@copilot continue ...` on the PR (the comment ends with the marker `CONTINUE_MARK`), at most `MAX_CONTINUE` (3) times; when Copilot failed before it started any work, the queue holds the issue for a person at once. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:568-574`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1114-1118`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1252-1305`; `codebase-analysis/ledger/issues/assemble.md` (the folder is the tracker's `analysis` setting, default `codebase-analysis`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:706`) |
| 8 | A person reviews and merges the assembly PR to the default branch (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1083-1103` |
| 9 | Queue closes the assembly issue and creates a verification issue using `verify_model`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1029-1031`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1100`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1119-1130` |
| 10 | Verification agent opens a PR with the whole-analysis report; the same continuation rule applies, with `verification-report.md` as the end marker. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:568-574`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1114-1118`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1260-1262` |
| 11 | A person reviews and merges the verification PR (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1083-1103` |
| 12 | Queue reads the report. A report that is missing, unreadable or not accepted (`FAIL`, a major correction without a fully confirmed re-check, or a `PASS AFTER CORRECTIONS` without a re-check) is not the end of the run: the queue labels the verification issue `bible-needs-revision`, comments, and reports "corrections asked ... revision next". An issue the queue sees still open (its merged pull request has not closed it) is also closed as not planned; an issue GitHub has already closed as completed is only labelled and commented (assumed: GitHub closes the issue when the pull request saying "Fixes #N" is merged, as the comment at lines 1038-1039 says). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1088-1099`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1037-1041`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1072-1076` |
| 13 | Next check, `revise_all_step`: the queue creates a `bible-revise-all` issue for Copilot that asks it to use the skill in revision mode on the whole analysis, apply every correction of `verification-report.md` without editing it, and finish with `status.py --write`. A revision pull request may change only files under the analysis folder, never `verification-*` files, else it is retried or held. A person merges it (inferred: the module docstring at line 28, and `merge` is called only at line 965, for session pull requests into the component branch), the queue closes the revise-all issue, and the next whole verification issue is created. A finished revise-all session that ends unfinished is continued as in step 7, with `status.json` as the end marker. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1172-1250`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1199-1203`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1219-1224`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1241-1250` |
| 14 | An accepted report ends the run only when three things hold: `accepted` is true for it (see the rules in [the queue component's R-19](../lld/bible-mode-b/README.md#business-rules)), the fingerprint printed in the report equals the fingerprint of the whole analysis on the default branch now (`status.py --fingerprint` on a downloaded tarball), and the report on the default branch is the one written by a merged pull request of this run's own verification issue. An accepted report that is not about the pages now, or not by this run, is labelled `bible-stale-verdict` and verified again. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1037-1071`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1010-1025`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:523-542` |
| 15 | At the Done step the queue reads the paths recorded on the tracker while the run was open (inferred: a search of the queue for `deferred_updates(` finds 4 hits, the definition, the two calls at lines 1133 and 1138 and one in `replay_closed_runs` at line 690) (see flow 5) and creates their update issues; then it comments "Done" and closes the tracker, reads the recorded paths once more, and creates update issues for any that arrived after the first read. An error in the first step is not caught there: the tracker stays open and the next check tries again; an error in the late step is commented on the closed tracker with the files to update by hand, and returns without the mark and label. When the late step did not fail, the queue comments `Recorded code changes: <n>, in update issues.` with `REPLAYED_MARK` and labels the tracker `bible-replayed`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1131-1137`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1138-1148`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1150-1162`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:672-675` |

**Failure paths:** A whole verification that is missing, unreadable or not accepted does not stop for a person: it starts the revision loop in steps 12-13. On the verdict alone, a person is asked only after `MAX_VERIFY_ROUNDS` (2) whole verifications without an accepted, current report (verdicts that asked for corrections plus stale ones, counted since a person last released the run): the queue creates the issue "the whole analysis needs a person" with the labels `bible-hold`, `bible-whole` and `bible-needs-human`; removing the label starts new rounds (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:76`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1187-1195`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1234-1240`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1164-1170`). A fingerprint that cannot be computed now is counted, and after `MAX_NOCHECK` (3) checks in a row a person is asked; when too little of the run's time is left the check waits for the next run (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1055-1062`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:89`). A held assembly, revision or verification session, a failed start, or a session that does not start within 30 minutes follows the same retry and hold rules as a component session, except that when a person releases a held whole-analysis session it is assigned to Copilot again, where a released component session is closed as not planned and its next step is decided afresh (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1104-1118`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1197-1225`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:618-628`). A pull request file list that cannot be completed raises a `RuntimeError` that is not caught here (inferred: `assemble_phase` and `revise_all_step` have no `except` around those calls, lines 1027-1148 and 1172-1250, except the late replay at 1139-1145), so that tracker's run ends with a logged error and is tried again at the next check (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1050`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1219`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:672-675`).

heading_path: 5. Changed code produces component delta issues
text:
## 5. Changed code produces component delta issues

**Trigger:** A push on the default branch that changes any file outside `codebase-analysis/**` and `.github/skills/**` (assumed: GitHub's `paths-ignore` filter). **Outcome:** While an analysis run is open (its tracker updated in the last 14 days) the change is only recorded on the tracker, and its update issues are created when the run ends through its Done step; if a person closes the tracker, or the run never finishes, `replay_closed_runs` creates them at a later check (inferred: a search of the file for `deferred_updates(` finds calls at `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:690`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1133` and `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1138`), and a later update issue for the same component asks for every change since the baseline (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1371-1375`); otherwise the queue maps the changed paths to components and creates one update issue per affected component, or one hold issue when more than 10 components changed.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Git as GitHub push event
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Queue as bible-queue.py
  participant API as GitHub API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Git->>Actions: Push on default branch
  Actions->>Actions: Checkout full history and write changed.txt
  Actions->>Queue: Run delta with changed-file path
  alt a tracker is open (updated in the last 14 days)
    Queue->>API: Comment the changed paths on the tracker (bible-deferred-update)
    Note over Queue,API: The update issues are created when the run reaches its Done step, or later by the replay of closed trackers
  else no open run
    Queue->>API: Read components.json and baseline.json
    alt either is missing on the default branch
      Queue->>Queue: Log that there is nothing to update, create nothing
    else both found
      Queue->>Queue: Map changed source paths to component names
      alt more than 10 components changed
        Queue->>API: Create one hold issue, no update session
      else 10 or fewer
        Queue->>API: Skip duplicate or create delta issue
        API-->>Agent: Assign new issue
      end
    end
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Push workflow runs for default-branch changes (job condition) and ignores only `codebase-analysis/**` and `.github/skills/**`; a push that changes workflows or queue code under `.github/` starts it (assumed: GitHub's `paths-ignore` filter). | `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:6-12`, `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:19` |
| 2 | Workflow checks out full history and writes changed paths to `$RUNNER_TEMP/changed.txt`. | `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:20-25`, `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:34-37` |
| 3 | CLI reads nonempty path lines and passes them to `Queue.delta`. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1426-1428` |
| 4 | When a tracker issue is open and its own `Updated` line (its creation time when it has none) is no older than 14 days (`ABANDONED_AFTER`), the queue does not create update issues: it comments the plain paths on the first such tracker, in comments of at most 200 paths, each with a hidden `bible-deferred-update` marker, and returns. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1324-1340`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:392-393` |
| 5 | The update issues for those paths are created when the run ends through its Done step: the assembly phase reads the marked comments the queue itself wrote, runs the update for them before it closes the tracker, and once more for paths recorded after the first read. For a tracker that a person closes, or a run that never reaches Done, `reconcile` calls `replay_closed_runs` after its loop over open trackers: for each closed tracker without the label `bible-replayed` and without the queue's own mark comment it reads the recorded paths and calls `delta` (which records them on a run that is open then, or creates the update issues), comments with `REPLAYED_MARK` and labels the tracker; a tracker for which this raises is tried again at the next check. The replay goes through `delta`: with no `components.json` or no `ledger/baseline.json` on the default branch the paths are dropped with only a log line, more than 10 touched components give one hold issue, and a component that already has an open update issue is skipped. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:667`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:676-679`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:681-703`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1131-1148`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1150-1162`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1371-1375`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1341-1344`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1353-1362`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1368-1370` |
| 6 | With no open run, the queue requires `components.json` and `ledger/baseline.json` on the default branch. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1341-1344` |
| 7 | Queue maps changed source paths (not the analysis folder, not the skills folder) to component names with the toolkit's `components` helpers. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1345-1352`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1363-1367` |
| 8 | When more than `MAX_DELTA_ISSUES` (10) components are touched, the queue creates one hold issue labelled `bible-delta` and `bible-needs-human` (unless one is open) and starts no update session. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1353-1362`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:394` |
| 9 | Otherwise it skips a component that already has an open delta issue, or creates a new issue. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1368-1381` |
| 10 | GitHub assigns each newly created issue to Copilot (assumed: GitHub performs the assignment named in the request). | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1371-1380` |

heading_path: 5. Changed code produces component delta issues
text: **Failure paths:** The first push with no prior SHA exits without a delta run. Missing catalog or baseline makes the queue log that there is nothing to update. Empty paths or paths outside component ownership produce no issue; an already-open delta issue is not duplicated; a push that touches more than 10 components gives a hold issue instead of update sessions (`.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:34-38`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1341-1344`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1353-1362`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1368-1381`). While a run is open the update waits for the run's Done step; if the tracker is closed by a person or the run never finishes, `replay_closed_runs` creates the update issues at a later check, and an update issue for the same component created meanwhile asks for every change since the baseline (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:681-697`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1371-1375`). A paths-ignored push, or one that changes only the analysis or the skills, does not start the workflow at all (assumed: GitHub's `paths-ignore` filter) (`.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:10-12`).

heading_path: 6. Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog
text:
## 6. Order total and stock validation use the in-process catalog

**Trigger:** Python caller invokes `order_total` and `validate`. **Outcome:** The caller receives a rounded total and a list of quantity/stock errors; `order_total` and `validate` persist no order or stock reservation (`components/orders/orders.py:23-42`).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Caller as Python caller
  participant Orders as orders.py
  participant Catalog as catalog.py
  Caller->>Orders: order_total(lines, loyal)
  loop each order line
    Orders->>Catalog: price_of(sku)
    alt known SKU
      Catalog-->>Orders: unit price
    else unknown SKU
      Catalog-->>Orders: KeyError, passed on to the caller
    end
  end
  Orders-->>Caller: rounded total using larger discount
  Caller->>Orders: validate(lines)
  loop each line
    alt quantity not positive
      Orders->>Orders: add the error quantity must be positive
    else quantity positive
      Orders->>Catalog: in_stock(sku, qty)
      alt stock too low or SKU unknown
        Catalog-->>Orders: false, the error not enough stock is added
      else enough stock
        Catalog-->>Orders: true
      end
    end
  end
  Orders-->>Caller: error list
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Caller supplies `(sku, qty)` lines and a loyalty flag. | `components/orders/orders.py:23-24` |
| 2 | `order_total` requests each line's price from `catalog.price_of`. | `components/orders/orders.py:19-25` |
| 3 | Catalog returns the price for a known SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:32-37` |
| 4 | `order_total` selects the larger loyalty/bulk discount and returns the rounded total. | `components/orders/orders.py:14-16`, `components/orders/orders.py:26-32` |
| 5 | Caller invokes `validate` on the lines. | `components/orders/orders.py:35` |
| 6 | Validation rejects nonpositive quantities or asks the catalog whether stock is sufficient. | `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` |
| 7 | Catalog returns stock availability for the SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:39-41` |
| 8 | Validation returns one error string per invalid line; no stock is decremented or order record written. | `components/orders/orders.py:35-42` |

**Failure paths:** Unknown SKU raises `KeyError` during total calculation. Validation accumulates `"quantity must be positive"` or `"not enough stock"` errors for invalid lines (`components/catalog/catalog.py:32-41`; `components/orders/orders.py:23-42`).

heading_path: 7. Remote catalog client reads a price
text:
## 7. Remote catalog client reads a price

**Trigger:** Caller uses `remote_price` or `remote_line_total`; the repository's test starts the catalog service on loopback. **Outcome:** Client reads the JSON price and converts it to a float.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Client as catalog client
  participant Server as CatalogHandler
  participant Catalog as catalog.py
  Client->>Client: Read CATALOG_URL and percent-encode SKU
  Client->>Server: GET /price/SKU, HTTP
  Server->>Server: Decode URL path
  Server->>Catalog: price_of(sku)
  Catalog-->>Server: Price or KeyError
  alt known SKU
    Server-->>Client: 200 JSON price
  else unknown SKU
    Server-->>Client: 404 JSON error, raised by urlopen as HTTPError
  end
  Client-->>Client: Parse response price as float
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Client reads `CATALOG_URL` and quotes the SKU. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:14-21` |
| 2 | Client sends the request, with no body (assumed: library behaviour, `urlopen` then sends a GET), with its configured timeout (default 5 seconds). | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |
| 3 | Handler extracts the URL path. | `components/catalog/service.py:24-25` |
| 4 | Handler decodes the SKU and calls `price_of`. | `components/catalog/service.py:28-31` |
| 5 | Catalog returns a price or raises `KeyError` for an unknown SKU. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:32-36` |
| 6 | Server returns `200` with `sku` and `price`, or `404` with an error. | `components/catalog/service.py:28-34` |
| 7 | Client loads the JSON body and converts `price` to `float`. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:22-23` |

**Failure paths:** Unknown SKUs return 404, which `urlopen` surfaces as `HTTPError` (assumed: library behaviour, and the docstring at `components/orders/catalog_client.py:20` says the same); invalid JSON, missing fields, timeouts, and connection errors are not translated by the client (inferred: `remote_price` has no `except`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`). The HTTP client path has test callers only in this repository (inferred: a search of the repository outside the analysis folder and the skills for `remote_price` and `remote_line_total` finds 10 hits: callers only in `test_catalog_client.py`, and `remote_line_total` calling `remote_price` in `catalog_client.py` itself) (`components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:26-29`; `components/orders/test_catalog_client.py:37-62`).

## 8. Settlement sends an order amount

**Trigger:** Python caller invokes `settle(order_id, amount, dev=False)`. **Outcome:** It sends JSON and returns whether a received response has status 200.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Caller as Python caller
  participant Orders as orders.py
  participant Partner as Payment partner or dev fake
  Caller->>Orders: settle(order_id, amount, dev)
  Orders->>Orders: Select partner or localhost URL
  Orders->>Orders: Serialize order and amount as JSON
  Orders->>Partner: HTTP request with a JSON body
  Partner-->>Orders: HTTP response
  alt status 200
    Orders-->>Caller: True
  else any other status that is returned
    Orders-->>Caller: False
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Caller supplies the order identifier, amount, and optional development flag. | `components/orders/orders.py:45` |
| 2 | `dev=True` selects `localhost:8099`; otherwise the hard-coded partner URL is used. | `components/orders/orders.py:7-12`, `components/orders/orders.py:47` |
| 3 | Code serializes `order` and `amount` as JSON. | `components/orders/orders.py:48-49` |
| 4 | Code sends the request, a JSON body with no method set (assumed: library behaviour, `urllib` then sends a POST), with a 15-second timeout by default. | `components/orders/orders.py:45`, `components/orders/orders.py:49-50` |
| 5 | Partner returns an HTTP response. | `components/orders/orders.py:49-51` |
| 6 | Function returns whether the response status equals 200. | `components/orders/orders.py:50-51` |

**Failure paths:** Network and HTTP errors from `urlopen` propagate (assumed: library behaviour, `urlopen` raises `HTTPError` for an error status); a non-200 response that is returned yields `False`. No retry or idempotency key is shown (`components/orders/orders.py:45-51`).

## 9. Component plan, fanout and gate

**Trigger:** Local operator runs the planning command and then fans out issues; the gate is run for a component pass. **Outcome:** Plan JSON is generated, issues are opened, and each gate reports pass/failure.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Local operator
  participant Plan as plan.py
  participant Files as Repository files
  participant Fanout as fanout.sh
  participant GH as GitHub CLI
  participant Gate as gate.py
  Operator->>Plan: Run planner
  Plan->>Files: Read component Python files and tests
  Plan->>Files: Write codebase-analysis/plan.json
  Operator->>Fanout: Run with owner/repo and ENGINE
  Fanout->>Files: Read component names from plan.json
  Fanout->>GH: Create labels and component issues
  Operator->>Gate: Run selected component pass
  Gate->>Files: Read plan and component artifacts
  Gate->>Files: Run unittest discovery for pass 3
  alt artifacts complete and tests pass
    Gate-->>Operator: Print PASS
  else missing artifact, unresolved ASK, no new test or failing test
    Gate-->>Operator: Print FAIL and return a failing status
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator runs the planner. | `tools/plan.py:41-62` |
| 2 | Planner scans component Python files, functions, tests, and literal HTTP URLs. | `tools/plan.py:21-38` |
| 3 | Planner writes versioned JSON to `codebase-analysis/plan.json`. | `tools/plan.py:41-58` |
| 4 | Operator runs fanout with a repository and engine selection. | `tools/fanout.sh:2-8` |
| 5 | Fanout reads component names from `plan.json`. | `tools/fanout.sh:9` |
| 6 | Fanout creates labels and issues through `gh`. | `tools/fanout.sh:10-29` |
| 7 | Operator runs the component gate for a selected pass. | `tools/gate.py:81-92` |
| 8 | Gate reads the plan and component pass artifacts. | `tools/gate.py:42-65`, `tools/gate.py:86-108` |
| 9 | For pass 3, gate invokes unittest discovery. | `tools/gate.py:63-78` |
| 10 | Gate prints PASS/FAIL and returns its process status. | `tools/gate.py:23-26`, `tools/gate.py:109-117` |

**Failure paths:** File/AST/JSON errors stop the relevant tool (assumed: library behaviour, an unreadable file, an `ast.parse` error or a `json.loads` error raises and ends the program), except that an invalid `status.json` makes the gate print FAIL (`tools/gate.py:95-98`); the gate fails on missing artifacts, unresolved `ASK`, no new test functions, or failing tests. `fanout.sh` exits on command failure (assumed: shell behaviour of `set -e`) and rejects an unknown engine (`tools/plan.py:21-58`; `tools/gate.py:42-78`, `tools/gate.py:94-108`; `tools/fanout.sh:6`, `tools/fanout.sh:24-30`).

## 10. POC workflow creates and assigns a task issue

**Trigger:** Operator dispatches the standalone POC workflow. **Outcome:** A GitHub issue is created and assigned directly to Copilot; the workflow does not check out repository code (`.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:34-72`: its one step is the inline script).

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  actor Operator as Repository operator
  participant Actions as GitHub Actions
  participant Shell as POC shell and jq
  participant API as GitHub Issues API
  participant Agent as Copilot coding agent
  Operator->>Actions: Dispatch title, task, base and model
  Actions->>Shell: Pass inputs and secret through environment
  alt secret is missing
    Shell-->>Actions: Error message and exit 1, no request
  else secret is present
    Shell->>Shell: Build request.json without token
    Shell->>API: gh api POST issue with assignment fields
    API-->>Shell: Issue response
    Shell->>Shell: Write response.json and print issue details
    API-->>Agent: Assign issue to Copilot
  end
```

| Step | What happens | Evidence |
| ---: | --- | --- |
| 1 | Operator supplies required title, task, base branch and optional model. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:11-29` |
| 2 | Workflow passes input values and `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` into environment variables; the job performs no checkout. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:34-72` |
| 3 | Shell exits if the token is missing. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:49-53` |
| 4 | `jq` creates `request.json` with issue body, assignee and `agent_assignment`; the token is not included in the JSON payload. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:55-64` |
| 5 | `gh api` creates the issue. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:66-69` |
| 6 | GitHub returns the issue response. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:66-69` |
| 7 | Shell writes `response.json` and prints issue details. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:68-72` |
| 8 | GitHub assigns the issue to Copilot (assumed: GitHub performs the assignment named in the request). | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:65-72` |

**Failure paths:** Missing `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` exits before request creation; invalid input or API/CLI errors stop the job under `set -euo pipefail` (assumed: shell behaviour of `set -e` and `pipefail`). Nothing retries (inferred: a search of the workflow for `retry` finds 0 hits); the job is limited to 5 minutes (`timeout-minutes: 5`), and the workflow sets no timeout on the `gh api` call (inferred: lines 66-69 pass no timeout option and wrap the call in no `timeout` command) (`.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:37`, `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:66-69`).

# Cross-cutting concerns

## Authentication and authorisation

The GitHub automation authenticates API requests with a bearer token; the catalog and sample order endpoints have no application authentication (inferred: a search of `components` for `auth`, `authorization`, `login`, `password`, `token` and `jwt` finds 0 hits). The workflow jobs are restricted to the default branch where specified and declare `contents: read`, while the separate assignment token's repository permissions are configured outside this repository.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Uses `GH_TOKEN` in the GitHub API `Authorization` header. Plan, queue and delta workflows take it from `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` and check out the default branch before running the queue code. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:117-126`; `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:26-45`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:12-36`; `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:14-33` |
| POC assignment | Uses `BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` as `GH_TOKEN`; the workflow creates the issue through `gh api`. The workflow declares `contents: read` and performs no checkout (inferred: its one step, `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:38-72`, is the inline script). | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:4-8`, `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:31-46`, `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:66-69` |
| `catalog` | HTTP handlers do not authenticate requests. The server defaults to loopback, but `CATALOG_HOST` can change the bind address. The supplier-feed client sends no credentials and verifies the server certificate through `ssl.create_default_context()` (assumed: Python's default context verifies certificates and host names; the unit test asserts it, `components/catalog/test_catalog.py:25-27`). | `components/catalog/service.py:15-34`, `components/catalog/service.py:40-43`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:48-55` |
| `orders` | Settlement requests use plain HTTP; remote catalog requests use plain HTTP by default (`DEFAULT_CATALOG_URL`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11`; `CATALOG_URL` may override it); no client credentials or authorization headers are set. | `components/orders/orders.py:7-12`, `components/orders/orders.py:45-50`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |

Consistency: varies (4 variants)

## Secrets

The workflow token is passed to the process through an environment variable, not embedded in workflow source or the issue request payload. The repository code refers to secret names only (inferred: a search of the repository outside the analysis folder and the skills for `ghp_`, `github_pat_`, `BEGIN` private-key headers and `password` finds 0 hits); the secret value and its provisioning are external (assumed: GitHub stores the repository secret).

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Workflows map `secrets.BIBLE_ASSIGN_TOKEN` to `GH_TOKEN`, check it before running, and the API client sends it as a bearer token. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:43-53`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`; `.github/workflows/bible-delta.yml:26-38`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:122-126` |
| POC assignment | Shell checks the token; `jq` constructs `request.json` from input values and does not add the token to that JSON. | `.github/workflows/poc-assign-copilot.yml:40-63` |
| Sample application | No application secrets or credential configuration are shown in the catalog or orders modules. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:1-63`; `components/catalog/service.py:1-49`; `components/orders/orders.py:1-51`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:1-29` |

Consistency: varies (3 variants)

## Configuration

Configuration is split across workflow inputs, environment variables, and source constants; no environment profile or central settings service is declared (inferred: a search of `components`, `tools`, `.github/bible` and `.github/workflows` for `profile` finds 0 hits, and a listing of the 30 files outside the analysis folder and the skills shows no settings file). The architecture page's configuration table lists the known settings and defaults.

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `bible-mode-b` | Workflow inputs select components, models and concurrency; environment variables configure GitHub API access, the agent identity (`BIBLE_AGENT_LOGINS`, `BIBLE_AGENT_APP`), toolkit location, and optional clock/test settings. | `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:9-24`, `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:44-49`; `.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:31-37`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:34-36`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:61-66`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:114`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:381`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:561-563` |
| `catalog` | Bind address and port use `CATALOG_HOST` and `CATALOG_PORT`; supplier and image URLs are constants. | `components/catalog/service.py:40-43`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:8-9` |
| `orders` | Catalog base URL uses `CATALOG_URL`; settlement URLs, discounts, bulk threshold and request timeout are function defaults or constants. | `components/orders/catalog_client.py:11`, `components/orders/catalog_client.py:14-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:7-16`, `components/orders/orders.py:45-50` |
| `tools` | Fanout reads `ENGINE` with default `copilot`; plan and gate paths are repository-local. | `tools/fanout.sh:2-12`, `tools/fanout.sh:24-29`; `tools/plan.py:41-58`; `tools/gate.py:81-108` |

## Error handling and resilience

The sample modules generally expose network and data errors to callers (`components/catalog/catalog.py:48-55`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`); the queue translates GitHub request failures and isolates reconciliation errors per tracker (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:133-139`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:672-675`). Session failures get one retry before a human hold (a start Copilot refuses is held at once, with no retry) (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:634-661`), but network requests have no general retry policy (inferred: a search of `components`, `tools` and `.github/workflows` for `retry`, `retries`, `backoff` and `tenacity` finds 0 hits, and the 17 hits in `.github/bible/bible_queue.py` are comments, messages and the session retry `fail_or_retry`, none around a request). An assembly or whole-analysis session that ends without its end marker is continued up to three times, and is held for a person at once when GitHub records that Copilot's work failed before it started (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:84`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1277-1286`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:1289-1295`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:128-140`).

| Component | How | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `catalog` | Unknown products raise `KeyError` in `price_of`; the HTTP handler returns 404 for that error. Supplier-fetch errors, a refused redirect to `http://` (an `HTTPError`) and feed parsing errors are not caught here. | `components/catalog/catalog.py:32-36`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:18-24`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:48-55`, `components/catalog/catalog.py:58-63`; `components/catalog/service.py:28-34` |
| `orders` | Validation returns per-line errors; unknown SKUs in totals and HTTP/transport errors from settlement or remote price lookup propagate to the caller. | `components/orders/orders.py:23-42`, `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23` |
| `bible-mode-b` | GitHub HTTP and transport errors become `RuntimeError`; reconciliation catches an exception per tracker. Failed agent work is retried once, then labelled for human attention; a start Copilot refuses is held at once. | `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:133-139`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:672-675`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:642-661`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:634-641` |
| `tools` | Gate reports missing or invalid artifacts and failing tests as failures; shell fanout stops on command errors. | `tools/gate.py:42-78`, `tools/gate.py:94-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:6`, `tools/fanout.sh:24-30` |

Request timeouts are explicit for GitHub API calls (60 seconds by default, with a 300-second tarball timeout), catalog price lookup (5 seconds), settlement (15 seconds), and supplier feed (10 seconds). There are no retries around these request calls (inferred: a search of `components`, `tools` and `.github/workflows` for `retry`, `retries`, `backoff` and `tenacity` finds 0 hits, and the 17 hits in `.github/bible/bible_queue.py` are comments, messages and the session retry `fail_or_retry`, none around a request); the orders settlement and the catalog price calls are single `urlopen` calls, the supplier call is a single `opener.open` call, and `GitHub.call` raises on failure; a component whose call raises is tried again at the next scheduled queue run; the queue's one retry is for failed agent sessions, not network requests (`.github/bible/bible_queue.py:741-744`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:117`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:298`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:642-661`; `components/orders/catalog_client.py:19-23`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-50`; `components/catalog/catalog.py:48-55`).

Consistency: varies (4 variants)

## Logging, metrics, and tracing

The queue writes progress and error messages to standard output; the catalog HTTP server suppresses its request log messages. No metrics or distributed tracing mechanism is present in the inspected source and workflow configuration (inferred: a search of `components/`, `tools/`, `.github/bible/` and `.github/workflows/` for `metric`, `statsd`, `prometheus`, `trace` and `opentelemetry` finds 0 hits).

| `catalog` | `CatalogHandler.log_message` is a no-op. | `components/catalog/service.py:36-37` |
| Sample application and tools | No logging framework, metrics, or tracing calls were found in the repository sweep (inferred: a search of `components`, `tools`, `.github/bible` and `.github/workflows` for `logging` and `logger` finds 0 hits, and for `metric`, `statsd`, `prometheus`, `trace` and `opentelemetry` 0 hits). | `codebase-analysis/progress.md` (Sweep: Outbound Python, Entry points, and Security dispositions) |

## Build, deployment, and dependencies

The sample application and tools run from source without a declared package build (inferred: a listing of the 30 files outside the analysis folder and the skills shows no build file, and a search of `components`, `tools`, `.github/bible` and `.github/workflows` for `build` finds 0 hits); GitHub Actions uses `ubuntu-latest` runners (assumed: GitHub-hosted runners). The repository's application and queue code use Python's standard library, while workflows also invoke GitHub Actions, `gh`, and `jq`.

No application packaging or deployment manifest is identified in the component pages. | `components/catalog/service.py:1-12`, `components/catalog/service.py:40-49`; `components/orders/orders.py:1-5`; `codebase-analysis/lld/catalog/README.md`; `codebase-analysis/lld/orders/README.md` |

# bible-mode-b test: agent context

Generated from the analysis of the code as it stood at the 2026-11-24 baseline (the queue file has 1,434 lines), depth deep. The code is the source of truth: open the cited lines before acting on any statement here.

Limits: Calls through dynamic dispatch, callbacks, reflection, string-built names, or another language may not appear in the graph; an absent `CALLS` edge is not proof of no call. `name-unique` and `analysis` edges depend on their resolution and the analysis, so treat them as leads to check. The graph and chunks describe this snapshot; after code changes, refresh the inventory, revise affected pages, and rerun `knowledge.py` (`.github/skills/analyzing-a-codebase/references/knowledge.md`).

## What the system is

The sample catalog/orders application sits beside GitHub Actions tooling that helps repository maintainers create and verify component analyses (`README.md:1-7`; `.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-8`). Repository operators dispatch runs and reviewers inspect pull requests or answer on session pull requests; no customer audience for the sample app is declared (inferred: a search of the repository outside the analysis folder and the skills for "customer" and "shopper" finds 0 hits) (`.github/workflows/bible-plan.yml:7-8`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:779-780`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:799-807`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:943-947`). The four components are catalog, orders, `bible-mode-b`, and tools: they provide product lookups/orders, analysis queueing, and planning/gate/fanout functions (`components/catalog/catalog.py:18-63`; `components/orders/orders.py:19-51`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:9-11`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:560-1381`; `tools/plan.py:21-62`; `tools/gate.py:42-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31`). The catalog has an optional HTTP server that binds the `host` argument of `make_server`, else `CATALOG_HOST`, else `127.0.0.1`; an empty `CATALOG_HOST` binds all interfaces (assumed: library behaviour of an empty host string in a socket address) (`components/catalog/service.py:40-43`, `components/catalog/service.py:40-49`); queue jobs run in GitHub Actions on `ubuntu-latest` runners (assumed: GitHub-hosted runners), and tools expose local CLI/shell entry points (`.github/workflows/bible-queue.yml:19-37`; `tools/plan.py:41-62`; `tools/gate.py:81-117`; `tools/fanout.sh:1-31`). Product data is process-local, orders has no durable order store (inferred: `orders.py` imports only `json`, `urllib.request` and the catalog, `components/orders/orders.py:2-5`), and queue state lives in GitHub issues, labels, branches, and pull requests (`components/catalog/catalog.py:11-15`; `components/orders/orders.py:45-51`; `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:128-154`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:407-427`, `.github/bible/bible_queue.py:705-756`).
